analysis: This is a rare case where the model thinks the market has the favorite priced too high. Miami is a home underdog getting a massive number -- DraftKings has it at +10.5, with Caesars and BookMaker.eu even more generous to the Dolphins at +11.5 -- but the model's own projected margin for the Chiefs is only 5.8 points, well short of either number. No injuries were found for either side this cycle, so this isn't an injury-driven read, just a straightforward Elo-vs-market gap on a big number.

That's the kind of divergence worth a second look precisely because 10.5-11.5 is a lot of points to lay, and 66.5% of sim runs have Miami covering the market number -- the model isn't saying Kansas City loses, just that this number is more than the matchup supports on paper.

leans.reasoning: Model margin (5.8) sits well inside the market's 10.5-11.5 range (DraftKings at the low end, Caesars/BookMaker.eu at the high end), and 66.5% of sims have Miami covering -- a real gap, though only a single signal with no injury confirmation.
